q1: SELECT ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR GROUP BY ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID HAVING COUNT(*)>=3
q2: SELECT D1.ACTOR_ID, D1.DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR D1 GROUP BY ACTOR_ID, DIRECTOR_ID HAVING COUNT(DIRECTOR_ID) >=3
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR GROUP BY ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID HAVING COUNT(*)>=3
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT D1.ACTOR_ID, D1.DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR D1 GROUP BY ACTOR_ID, DIRECTOR_ID HAVING COUNT(DIRECTOR_ID) >=3
explanation: Both Q1 and Q2 group the ACTORDIRECTOR table by ACTOR_ID and DIRECTOR_ID, and apply a HAVING condition that counts the number of rows per group. In Q1, COUNT(*) counts all rows in the group, while in Q2, COUNT(DIRECTOR_ID) counts the number of non-null values of DIRECTOR_ID in the group. Since DIRECTOR_ID is part of the GROUP BY clause and not null in the table, COUNT(*) and COUNT(DIRECTOR_ID) will produce the same result in this context. Hence, the queries are semantically equivalent.
